study_identification_part.si4_title: Effects of anterior temporal lobe resection on cortical morphology

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To examine the effects of anterior temporal lobe resection (ATLR) on brain morphology in individuals with temporal lobe epilepsy using both traditional and recently developed independent morphological measures (K, I, and S) in a surface-based analysis.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Subject-wise centered differences between pre- and postoperative morphological measures; SurfStat random field theory clustering with cluster-wise significance threshold p ≤ 0.05; effect sizes measured in Cohen's f²
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper describes using subject-wise centering to enable pairwise analysis of changes, then applying SurfStat's random field theory approach with cluster-wise correction for multiple comparisons at p ≤ 0.05. Effect sizes are reported as Cohen's f².
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: To allow for a pairwise analysis of the changes between the pre- and postoperative scans, we centred the data subject-wise at each vertex. We used the Matlab toolbox SurfStat (Worsley et al., 2009) for a surface based statistical analysis that corrects for multiple comparison and accounts for spatial correlation with random field theory. ... We repeated this for all six variables (traditional and independent), ending up with a surface map of the pairwise effect between the two scans for each. We applied a threshold for effects having a cluster-wise model significance of p ≤ .05. We reported effects measured in Cohen's f².

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Surface-based paired analysis of pre- vs postoperative morphological changes using SurfStat random field theory clustering (cluster-wise p ≤ 0.05); separate ipsilateral and contralateral analyses combining left and right onset groups; covariate effects tested separately for age at surgery, duration since first seizure, resection volume, side of resection, time between surgery and postoperative scan, and seizure outcome (ILAE 1&2 vs 3+) using design matrices; subject-wise differences between pre- and postoperative scans used for covariate testing
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ATLR caused widespread morphological changes mainly in regions near the resection (orbitofrontal and inferior frontal gyri, pre-/postcentral gyri, supramarginal gyrus, lateral occipital and lingual cortex) and also remotely in contralateral regions (lateral occipital cortex, inferior frontal gyrus, frontal pole), with independent morphological measures revealing additional effects not detected by traditional measures; no significant covariate effects were found.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: ATLR resulted in significant morphological changes in both traditional and independent measures. Ipsilaterally, the orbitofrontal and inferior frontal gyri showed increased total and exposed surface area, increased isometric term I, increased shape complexity S, and decreased tension K, likely due to cortical sagging into the resection cavity. The ipsilateral lateral occipital and lingual cortex showed decreased cortical thickness and exposed area, increased K, and decreased I. The ipsilateral pre-/postcentral gyri showed increased thickness, while the supramarginal gyrus showed increased K. Contralaterally, the lateral occipital cortex showed increased thickness, total area, K, and I, while the inferior frontal gyrus and frontal pole showed increased total area, K, and I. Some effects (e.g., supramarginal gyrus) were only visible in independent measures, particularly K, while some thickness changes (e.g., precentral gyrus) were not reflected in independent measures. The affected regions were structurally connected to the resected temporal lobe via white matter tracts previously shown to have altered diffusion metrics post-ATLR. None of the tested covariates (age at surgery, TLE duration, resection volume, resection side, time to postoperative scan, seizure outcome) showed significant effects on morphological changes at cluster significance of 0.05. The mean scaling law slope in TLE patients was 1.246, confirming the universal scaling law applies to this cohort.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Sample size and lack of covariate effects; inability to analyze insula and corpus callosum due to method limitations; inability to definitively determine if changes represent atrophy or reorganization/compensation; lack of correlation analysis with postsurgical deficits and functional outcomes; limited age range (19-60 years); exclusion of ipsilateral temporal lobe from analysis prevents assessment of focal abnormalities
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: The method of correcting surface areas does not perform well for regions that are particularly flat or located in deep sulci, so some vertices were missing data. Where possible, we imputed data on vertices that were missing values as the mean over their direct neighbouring vertices, but had to exclude the insula and the regions around the corpus callosum from our analysis, since these regions had entirely missing values. ... We cannot decisively determine if morphological change is a sign of atrophy or reorganisation, or potentially even increased function to compensate for the loss of tissue. ... Further studies linking structural changes to postsurgical deficits such as visual field impairment will be necessary to deduce the nature of the processes causing the changes to morphology after ATLR. ... although as subjects in our study were in an age range of 19 – 60 years, there might be age-dependent effects for individuals outside this range. ... One may hypothesise that abnormalities in morphological measures could be useful for localisation during pre-surgical evaluation with the biggest changes pertaining to seizure-freedom located within the ipsilateral anterior temporal lobe, which was excluded from our analyses.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Study used novel independent morphological measures (K, I, S) derived from universal scaling law of cortical folding to capture morphological information not revealed by traditional measures due to their covariance; separate analyses conducted for ipsilateral and contralateral hemispheres by combining left and right onset groups (see supplementary materials for onset-specific results); temporal lobe excluded from analysis bilaterally to avoid resection cavity effects; normative model automatically accounts for healthy aging between pre- and postoperative scans; controls processed twice (with/without temporal lobes) to match patient hemisphere-specific analyses

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study is unique in applying normative modeling to longitudinal surgical data rather than cross-sectional case-control comparison. The normative model serves to debias the data and account for healthy aging effects between scans (median 3.6 months postoperative interval, range 2-13 months). The study introduces and validates independent morphological measures (K=tension, I=isometric scaling, S=shape complexity) derived from the universal scaling law of cortical folding as alternatives to traditional measures (thickness, total area, exposed area). The scaling law was verified in TLE patients pre-surgery (mean slope 1.246, expected 1.25). Follow-up scans were 2-13 months post-surgery with pre-surgery scans up to 3 years before surgery. Data availability: NKI dataset public; patient data planned for 2023/2024 release; de-identified morphological summary data available on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.7957831); analysis code on GitHub (cnnp-lab/2023Leiberg_ATLRmorphology). The study used restricted maximum likelihood for smoothing parameter estimation in GAMM. Seizure outcome was classified by ILAE scale at 12 months post-surgery. Median TLE duration: left TLE 19 years (IQR 27.99), right TLE 21.5 years (IQR 21.23). Seizure outcome group 3+ (recurrent seizures): left TLE n=12, right TLE n=11. Two scanning protocols used: protocol 1 (0.94×0.94×1.1 mm, n=52 patients, n=22 controls); protocol 2 (1×1×1 mm, n=49 patients, n=69 controls).
